defects.title: Game-level odds endpoint writes zero rows
defects.root_cause: market_capture_run.py's _poll_and_write() filtered the slate-wide /odds response with `rows = [r for r in rows if r["game_id"] == game_id]`, where `game_id = game["game_id"]` is OUR internal league/PROV id (e.g. "1022600230", as seen in poll_log.csv), while every row flatten_odds_payload() produces carries the VENDOR's own event id (a hex uuid, e.g. "58beff9061f15ff3f416542cb51f4751") as row["game_id"] -- confirmed by direct comparison against the props branch, which resolves and filters on the same vendor id via the /events team-name lookup and works. The two id spaces never intersect, so the filter reduced every poll's nonempty parsed row list to zero BEFORE validate_row/append ran -- exactly reproducing the measured symptom (HTTP 200, n_rows_written=0, n_rows_rejected=0, no error, on all 21 measured polls) with no data-availability or parsing failure involved.
defects.exact_change: In market_capture_run.py's _poll_and_write(): resolve `event_id = events_by_teams.get((game['home'], game['away']))` (the same free /events lookup the props branch already used) BEFORE fetching/filtering, and filter game-odds rows on `r['game_id'] == str(event_id)` instead of the internal game_id. If no event_id resolves, the slate-wide response cannot be honestly attributed to this game at all (the endpoint is not scopeable to one game) -- this is now recorded as an explicit SKIPPED reason in poll_log.csv rather than another silent zero.

defects.title: All books share one byte-identical retrieval_ts per poll
defects.root_cause: Two independent causes, closed separately: (a) market_capture_run.py computed ONE retrieval_ts before making BOTH the game-odds HTTP call and the props HTTP call, then reused that single value for every row from either call -- so even two genuinely sequential network round trips shared one timestamp, a pure code artifact with no vendor excuse. (b) Within a SINGLE HTTP response, The Odds API bundles every subscribed bookmaker into one JSON payload -- there is no per-book endpoint variant and no per-book timing field in the response; this is a genuine vendor-shape constraint, not a code defect.
defects.exact_change: fetch_odds_snapshot/fetch_event_props_snapshot now capture the wall-clock instant immediately after each HTTP response is received (inside a new `_timing()` helper) and return it as part of a `timing` dict (4th return value); _poll_and_write now takes `retrieval_ts = timing['response_received_ts']` per call instead of one value shared across both calls. This closes cause (a). Cause (b) was NOT changed: no per-book HTTP call splitting or per-book parse-order stamping was implemented -- see decision_packet below for why.

cause_a_closed: tests_M26.py::test_defect2_odds_and_props_calls_get_distinct_retrieval_ts -- end-to-end against the current _poll_and_write; asserts the odds-call rows and props-call rows carry disjoint retrieval_ts sets. PASS.

Real bytes (same live_verify_defect1.py run as defect 1): poll_log.csv shows poll_ts=2026-08-07T14:03:04.828587Z for the odds call and poll_ts=2026-08-07T14:03:04.923875Z for the props call -- genuinely distinct, ~95ms apart, matching real sequential network round-trip time.
cause_b_documented_not_closed: tests_M26.py::test_defect2_within_one_payload_books_still_share_one_timestamp_documented -- asserts that within one HTTP response (2+ books, e.g. draftkings+fanduel), exactly ONE retrieval_ts is still shared across all books' rows. This test is intentionally written to FAIL if a future change silently 'fixes' this by fabricating per-book parse-order timestamps -- which would carry zero real cross-book ordering information (JSON array order is vendor-arbitrary and typically stable poll-to-poll, so a parse-loop stamp would produce a fake, constant 'fastest book' ranking) and would be a Severity-A-adjacent measurement-integrity regression, not a fix. PASS (documents the limitation, does not close it).

defects.decision_packet: Closing cause (b) for real would require either (i) per-book-scoped HTTP calls (The Odds API's documented `bookmakers=` filter param would let a request scope to one bookmaker), which multiplies the odds-call request COUNT by the number of tracked books (5 in the current live tape, up to 11 observed in the live verification run) -- i.e. roughly a 5-11x increase in vendor-credit consumption for the game-odds leg of every poll, a materially different cost/rate profile than the M00-ruled ceilings were sized against; or (ii) fabricating per-book timestamps from JSON parse order, which this node determined would be actively misleading (see test above) and refused to implement. Per this node's hard constraints ('no poll rate raised above the ceilings already ruled' -- interpreted here as covering request-volume/quota burn rate, not only polling cadence) and stop conditions ('a fix would require raising poll rates beyond ceilings ... record it as a decision packet instead'), this node did not implement (i) unilaterally. Recommends: a coordinator/user decision on whether the 5-11x credit-consumption increase for per-book game-odds polling is acceptable before implementing (i); this node's code is otherwise ready to be extended that way if authorized.
defects.status: PARTIALLY_CLOSED -- cause (a) CLOSED, cause (b) NOT_CLOSED_WITH_REASON (vendor payload shape + poll-rate/quota-ceiling decision required, recorded above as a decision packet)

defects.title: Neither writer can witness a suspension / vanish-and-return
defects.root_cause: Two writers, two distinct structural gaps, both verified by full reads of the code (matching M17's own audit): (a) market_snapshot_writer.py's flatten_odds_payload/flatten_props_payload only ever emit a row for a (book, market, outcome) that IS present in the current poll's response; a chain that silently drops out of the vendor's payload between polls produces NO row at all -- absence was indistinguishable from 'never checked'. Also confirmed: the Odds API response shape genuinely carries no book-suspended flag distinct from 'not returned', so 'suspended' cannot be honestly assigned from this vendor -- 'missing' is the ceiling label, matching M17's own finding. (b) capture_sxbet.py's SxBetClient.get_active_markets() calls /markets/active exclusively, an endpoint that by construction only returns currently-active markets (100% ACTIVE census, confirmed), and build_envelope() only writes a row when a marketHash's content SHA-256 changes -- so a market that vanishes from /markets/active and later reappears with byte-identical content produces zero rows on either edge of the transition (no removal event, no reappearance event).
defects.exact_change: (a) market_snapshot_writer.py gains RosterIndex (persists which (game_id,book,market,outcome) chains were market_status=active as of the last poll processed under a given roster_key) and detect_vanished_chains() (diffs the current poll's active chains against the roster and synthesizes an explicit market_status='missing' row -- never 'suspended' -- for anything that vanished, with the real witnessed retrieval_ts of the poll that noticed the absence). Wired into market_capture_run.py's _poll_and_write for BOTH the odds branch (roster_key=f'{game_id}:odds') and the props branch (roster_key=f'{game_id}:props', explicitly guarded to skip when the props call returned HTTP 422/no data, so a we-failed-to-get-a-normal-response is never misread as a mass vanish). (b) capture_sxbet.py gains compute_roster_transitions() (diffs this cycle's active marketHash set against the persisted StateStore roster, guarded to run ONLY when the /markets/active poll itself succeeded) and a new additive roster_events table/file, writing an explicit 'vanished' event on the active->absent edge and a 'reappeared' event on the absent->active edge -- written unconditionally (not through build_envelope's content-hash dedup), so a vanish-and-return with identical content, which the `markets` table's own dedup renders invisible, still leaves a trace in roster_events.

defects.title: Vendor-latency and clock-skew bounds unmeasured
defects.root_cause: Neither writer ever measured or recorded a vendor_latency_bound or clock_skew_bound anywhere -- M07 and M21 both independently confirmed vendor_latency_bound=UNBOUNDED and clock_skew_bound=UNMEASURED/CLOCK_UNBOUNDED for every tape they read. The amendment-4 per-row schema fields (vendor_ts, vendor_ts_semantics, retrieval_ts, ingestion_ts, max_staleness_bound, poll_interval_at_capture, vendor_latency_note, payload_hash, prev_snapshot_ref) were already all present and populated on every row of both tapes -- the gap was specifically that no code anywhere computed an actual latency or skew NUMBER; the fields existed structurally but nothing populated the two hardest ones.
defects.exact_change: Added, on both capture paths: (1) a witnessed round-trip time per HTTP call (rtt_seconds = wall-clock time from request-sent to response-received) as the measured, honestly-caveated vendor_latency_bound (upper-bounds vendor+network+our-own overhead combined -- explicitly NOT claimed to isolate vendor-only processing time, since neither vendor exposes a server-timing breakdown). (2) a clock-skew ESTIMATE derived from the HTTP `Date` response header vs. our own witnessed response-received time (estimate_clock_skew_seconds, whole-second resolution, explicitly caveated as conflating true clock skew with one-way network transit -- an upper bound, not an isolated skew value; returns None if the vendor omits a Date header). Odds API side: new additive vendor_timing_log.csv (never touches poll_log.csv's existing schema/header -- append-only holds). SX Bet side: the same two fields added directly onto poll_log.jsonl's existing per-call log rows (JSONL tolerates new keys on new rows without any header-migration risk, unlike the Odds API's fixed-header CSV).

defects.what_remains_unbounded_and_why: True isolated vendor-only processing latency (as opposed to round-trip time, which also includes network transit and our own request/response marshaling) -- neither vendor exposes a server-timing/processing-time header. Clock-skew resolution finer than whole seconds -- the HTTP Date header is the only clock-comparison signal either vendor offers; a tighter bound would need NTP-style synchronization or a vendor timestamp endpoint neither offers. Per-book latency/skew -- inherits the same single-payload-bundling limitation as defect 2.
defects.status: CLOSED (to the extent achievable from these two vendors without additional infrastructure; the residual gaps above are stated, not silently left)
